title: Solar Eclipse Nile Cruise — Luxor Roundtrip & Totality at Karnak
intro: Seven nights on the river, timed so the ship puts you back on the Luxor quay on the morning of the eclipse. The Monday sailing runs the full roundtrip — down through Esna, Edfu and Kom Ombo to Aswan, two nights there for the High Dam, Philae and the botanical garden, then back up the same water with the temples seen from the other direction. You wake in Luxor on 2 August, step off after breakfast, and go straight to Karnak for totality among the columns. Cairo bookends it: a night to land and sleep off the flight at the start, and on the last morning the Giza Plateau and the Grand Egyptian Museum before the airport. No clock-watching on board — the programme below is the shape of each day, and the ship keeps to it, not you.

arrival.title: Arrival in Cairo — Sunday 25 July
arrival.description:
Arrival at Cairo International Airport.
Meet & assist by our representative airside, who stays with you through the visa, passport and customs formalities and collects your luggage with you.
Private air-conditioned transfer to your hotel.
Nothing scheduled: the day is yours to sleep off the flight, eat, and adjust before an early start tomorrow.
Dinner at the hotel.
Overnight in Cairo.
arrival.hotel: Pyramids Park Resort Cairo, 4★ (or equal) — bed & breakfast

days.title: To Luxor & Embarkation — Monday 26 July
days.description:
Early breakfast at the hotel — or a breakfast box if the flight goes before service — and check-out.
Transfer to Cairo airport for the morning flight to Luxor, around an hour, met on arrival and driven straight to the mooring.
Embarkation before lunch. Your cabin is ready and the ship is home for the next seven nights.
Lunch on board, then the afternoon at leisure — the sundeck, the pool, or the town if you want it.
Afternoon tea.
A belly dancer in the lounge before an à la carte dinner on board.
Overnight moored in Luxor.
days.hotel: Blue Shadow Nile cruise (or equal) — full board

days.title: The West Bank, then Sailing to Esna — Tuesday 27 July
days.description:
Breakfast on board, then across to the west bank early with your private Egyptologist, ahead of the heat.
The Valley of the Kings: royal tombs cut deep into the hillside, their corridors of painted text and star-vaulted ceilings intact. Tutankhamun, Seti I and Nefertari are separately ticketed and can be added on the spot.
Medinet Habu, the mortuary temple of Ramses III — the best preserved on the bank, colour still sitting in the reliefs of the migdol gate.
The Temple of Queen Hatshepsut at El-Deir El-Bahari, three colonnaded terraces built straight into the cliff face.
The Colossi of Memnon, the two seated quartzite giants of Amenhotep III.
Back aboard and the ship sails for Esna over lunch, with the afternoon free as the banks turn to sugar cane and water buffalo.
Afternoon tea on the sundeck, then the captain's welcome cocktail, à la carte dinner and karaoke in the lounge.
Overnight moored at Esna.
days.hotel: Blue Shadow Nile cruise (or equal) — full board

days.title: Edfu & Kom Ombo — Wednesday 28 July
days.description:
The ship sails for Edfu through the Esna lock while you sleep; breakfast on board.
Mid-morning at the Temple of Horus at Edfu, reached by horse-drawn carriage from the mooring — the most completely preserved temple in Egypt, with its pylon, courtyard, black granite falcon and roofed sanctuary still holding the barque shrine.
Back aboard to sail on to Kom Ombo, with lunch under way and the afternoon at leisure.
A ship tour with the captain: the bridge, the engine room, and how a vessel this size is handled through a lock.
Afternoon tea, then a cooking class with the ship's chef — an Egyptian dish or two you can reproduce at home.
An oriental band and dinner buffet on the sundeck, then the galabia party. The ship lends you the robe.
Overnight moored at Kom Ombo.
days.hotel: Blue Shadow Nile cruise (or equal) — full board

days.title: Aswan — the High Dam, Philae & the Botanical Garden — Thursday 29 July
days.description:
The ship sails for Aswan overnight; breakfast on board.
The Aswan High Dam in the morning, the granite quarries and the lake behind it.
Then the Temple of Philae, reached by motor launch to Agilkia Island, where the whole complex was cut into blocks and rebuilt stone by stone to save it from the rising water — the last temple in Egypt where the old religion was practised.
Lunch on board.
Out onto the Nile by motor boat in the afternoon, through the granite islands and the cataract channel where the current still runs fast, to the Botanical Garden on Kitchener's Island.
Afternoon tea on your return, dinner on board, and a Nubian show in the lounge.
Overnight moored in Aswan.
days.hotel: Blue Shadow Nile cruise (or equal) — full board

days.title: Aswan at Leisure — Optional Abu Simbel — Friday 30 July
days.description:
The ship stays moored at Aswan all day and the programme is deliberately empty.
Optional, at extra cost, and this is the day for it: Abu Simbel. South across the desert to the two rock temples of Ramses II and Nefertari — four twenty-metre seated colossi cut into the cliff, and a sanctuary the whole mountain was sliced up and moved to save. By road or by short flight, quoted on request.
If you would rather stay: the souk, a felucca hour under the sail, the Nubian village across the water, or simply the sundeck and the pool.
Lunch on board whenever you get back, and the afternoon free.
Afternoon tea on the sundeck, the captain's cocktail, dinner on board and a Nubian show.
Overnight moored in Aswan.
days.hotel: Blue Shadow Nile cruise (or equal) — full board

days.title: North Again — Kom Ombo, Edfu & Esna — Saturday 31 July
days.description:
The ship casts off early for Kom Ombo; breakfast on board as you sail.
The Temple of Kom Ombo in the cool of the morning, right on the riverbank — the only double temple in Egypt, halved precisely between Sobek the crocodile and Haroeris the elder Horus, with the surgical instruments carved on the outer wall and the crocodile museum alongside.
Back aboard and on to Edfu, then Esna, with lunch served under way. This is the day the river gives you: the same water in the other direction, the banks passing, nothing to do.
Afternoon tea on the sundeck as the ship works down through the lock.
Dinner on board, then a galabia party.
Overnight moored at Esna.
days.hotel: Blue Shadow Nile cruise (or equal) — full board

days.title: Back to Luxor — Karnak & the East Bank — Sunday 1 August
days.description:
An early morning sail brings the ship up to Luxor; breakfast on board and the morning free as you come alongside.
Lunch on board.
The East Bank in the afternoon with your private Egyptologist. Karnak first: the avenue of ram-headed sphinxes, the first pylon, and the Great Hypostyle Hall — one hundred and thirty-four columns, the tallest twenty-one metres, still carrying their painted architraves. Your guide will walk the ground you will be standing on tomorrow.
Then Luxor Temple, joined to Karnak by the restored three-kilometre Avenue of Sphinxes, with the standing obelisk of Ramses II at the gate.
Afternoon tea, dinner on board and a belly dancer in the lounge.
An early night — tomorrow is the reason for the dates.
Overnight moored in Luxor.
days.hotel: Blue Shadow Nile cruise (or equal) — full board

days.title: Disembarkation, Totality at Karnak, and North to Cairo — Monday 2 August
days.description:
Breakfast on board, then disembarkation after breakfast with assistance and your luggage taken care of. Your bags travel with the vehicle for the rest of the day.
Straight to Karnak, early and on purpose: the approaches will be closed or crawling by mid-morning and we intend to be inside the precinct long before that.
You already know the complex from yesterday, so today is not a tour. Your guide settles you where you want to be — the great court, the sacred lake, or among the columns.
The partial phases run for over an hour. The light goes wrong, the temperature drops, the birds stop. Then totality, over the temple of Amun-Ra, on ground where the priesthood tracked exactly this for three thousand years. Luxor lies close to the point of greatest duration on this eclipse, one of the longest of the century.
We wait for the roads to clear rather than fight them, then a late lunch and the evening flight up to Cairo. A sleeper cabin on the night train is held as a fallback in case the flight moves.
Transfer to your hotel and a quiet night.
Overnight in Cairo.
days.hotel: Pyramids Park Resort Cairo, 4★ (or equal) — bed & breakfast

departure.title: Giza, the Grand Egyptian Museum & Departure — Tuesday 3 August
departure.description:
Breakfast at your hotel, then out early with your Cairo Egyptologist while the plateau is still cool.
The Giza Plateau, privately: the Great Pyramid of Khufu, the pyramids of Khafre and Menkaure, and the panoramic viewpoint where all three line up. Entry into the burial chamber is available on the spot at extra cost.
The Great Sphinx and the Valley Temple of Khafre.
The Grand Egyptian Museum: the hanging obelisk, the Ramses II atrium, the grand staircase of royal statuary, and the complete Tutankhamun collection — over five thousand objects with the death mask among them.
Time to eat and to buy anything you still want, with a late check-out held at the hotel so you can shower and change before you travel.
Private transfer to Cairo International Airport in good time for your international flight, with final meet & assist through check-in. Safe journey home.
